answer: Bandwidth Deprecation Tax scales transaction fees by network crowding, rising toward a cost zenith during peak congestion. When an agent spawns clones, the collective message volume triggers local congestion, inflating execution tolls for every linked sub-entity. An attacker pays this scaling penalty directly in processing fees, which ripple across their network cluster to make mass replication economically unviable past a tight threshold. Every new node must clear a crystal-clear pricing wall where marginal operational expenses outpace utility.
